Backend: new /app/backend/tests/test_team_staff.py (16 tests) covers staff creation via POST /api/admin/users, team listing, staff 403 on members/payments/monthly/create-user/patch-user/bulk-delete/remove-staff, staff 200 on stats (no revenue/members/active_members/gifts_sold keys), deals, businesses, top-deals, status changes, and staff session revocation after removal. Full regression: 100 passed, 1 skipped. Frontend (desktop 1920 + mobile 390): Deals page near-me-btn grants geolocation via Playwright permissions (Melbourne CBD), shows near-me-note, renders deal-distance-{id} chips (10/13 seed deals have lat/lng), toggles cleanly to clear state, shows near-me-error on permission denial, and works at 390px. Admin shell: owner sees Members/Payments/Team nav + revenue cards; staff login succeeds via /admin, sidebar shows exactly Overview/Deals/Businesses/Check-a-code (no members/payments/team), Overview hides all four money cards (revenue/members/active_members/gifts_sold) while Top deals widget renders, direct URLs /admin/members, /admin/payments, /admin/team all render admin-owner-only block for staff, Deals page has no deals-bulk-delete button, Businesses page has no add-business-btn. Main-site navbar shows 'Admin' link for staff (verified by screenshot). Created staff and removed via API cleanup.
critical_code_review_comments: server.py is 1706 lines — still worth splitting into routers (admin_users, admin_deals, admin_businesses, team, payments). Prior iterations already flagged this.

admin_remove_staff uses db.users.delete_one directly; on removal the staff's active refresh cookie is invalidated only because /auth/me returns 401 when the user record is gone — explicit session/token revocation would be safer if sessions are ever persisted.

AdminShell NAV filtering by ownerOnly is correct, but the route guards for /admin/members, /admin/payments, /admin/team rely on the OwnerOnly wrapper rendered inside the page component rather than route-level gates — fine today but easy to forget on a new owner-only page.

sortNearby uses a numeric subtract of booleans (b.open_now === true) - (a.open_now === true) which is clean, but deals.map mutates source objects via spread each render; harmless but worth memoising if the deals list grows.
